DOLOMITES · ALTA BADIA · OCT 2027

Four nights in the Dolomites, one base, a new valley each day.

Corvara in Alta Badia is the base. Tre Cime di Lavaredo and Lago di Braies, the Seceda cable car and Alpe di Siusi, then the Sella Ronda loop and Val di Funes. The larches are just starting to turn, so the colour builds through the stay. Lifts are thinning out for the season, but the passes stay open unless snow comes early. The last day is the drive to Venice, with a stop in Bolzano or Merano.

Worth knowing

This trip lands right at the start of the best-odds larch window, with color still building through the stay. Sellaronda-area lifts are thinning out for the season by now — the passes themselves stay open on drive-through unless snow hits early.

Fun fact

The Dolomites are named after Déodat de Dolomieu, the French mineralogist who first described this rock type in 1791. The pale peaks are literally fossilized coral reef — laid down in a tropical sea roughly 250 million years ago, then pushed skyward when Africa and Europe collided.

The hikes · badges rank priority (must-do / highly recommended / good to have) and describe the payoff · all four are day trips from Corvara
Adolf Munkel Trail (Via delle Odle)
Must-doThe Odle wall
5.7 mi / 9.2 km1,240 ft / 378 mEasy–Moderate3–3.5 hr3.4k reviews

Trailhead: Zannes/Zans car park, Val di Funes (1,680 m) — ~1.5 hr from Corvara via Passo Gardena and Ortisei, the longest day-trip drive of the stay. Parking: €8, cash only (€4 with a Dolomiti Card).
The path runs along the foot of the Odle/Geisler wall — the range this whole chapter is built around — passing three huts that serve lunch. The season runs early June to mid/late October and is snow-dependent, so mid-October is the tail end: check trail and hut status the week before.

↗ View on AllTrails
Col Raiser – Secèda – Pieralongia
Must-doRidge panorama
4.7 mi / 7.6 kmgondola does the climbModerate2 hr 45 min285 reviews

Trailhead: top station of the Col Raiser gondola, Santa Cristina — ~45 min from Corvara via Passo Gardena. Pass: gondola ticket.
The tilted Seceda ridge is the most photographed skyline in the Dolomites, and this loop adds the Alpe Mastlé pastures and the Pieralongia rock. The Col Raiser gondola shuts for the season in early November — mid-October is inside the window, but only just.

↗ View on AllTrails
Sass Pordoi – Piz Boè
Highly recommended3,000 m summit
3.3 mi / 5.3 km1,410 ft / 430 mModerate2–3.5 hr234 reviews

Trailhead: Sass Pordoi cable-car top station (2,950 m) at Passo Pordoi — ~30 min from Corvara via Passo Campolongo. Pass: cable-car ticket.
The most accessible 3,000 m summit in the Dolomites: the cable car does the climbing and Rifugio Capanna Fassa sits on the 3,152 m top. Not a stroll despite the short distance — there are steep scrambling steps with cables and some exposure, and it is properly cold and windy up there in October.

↗ View on AllTrails
Badia – Armentara – La Crusc
Good to haveMeadow & sanctuary
5.4 mi / 8.7 km2,552 ft / 778 mChallenging3–3.5 hr99 reviews

Trailhead: La Crusc 1 gondola valley station, Badia — ~10 min from Corvara, the one hike here that needs barely any drive. Pass: gondola ticket, or walk up and add the gain.
The Armentara meadows spread beneath the Sasso di Santa Croce, with the Santa Croce pilgrimage church at 2,045 m. Rated challenging for its 778 m of gain — riding both La Crusc gondolas up and walking down turns it into an easy afternoon.

Drive-through stopover · the same trick as Bergamo, applied again

Bolzano & Merano

  • Waltherplatz & old-town market stalls, Bolzano — an easy hour-plus stop
  • Törggelen tavern lunch — chestnuts and new wine
  • Merano, 30 min further — possibly the Saturday market day of the Merano Grape Festival (traditionally the third weekend of October, likely Oct 16–17, 2027)
The festival's parade is Sunday, after you've continued to Venice — a real trade-off, not a guarantee. Want the parade too? Trade one Venice night for an overnight in Merano instead.

Explore more in the Dolomites

Markets and nightlife are genuinely thin up here in October (the famous markets are Christmas markets, Nov–Jan) — flagged rather than padded. Nature is where this region delivers.
